text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No generative AI or personal data review recorded","detail":"The proposal uses an LLM (generative AI) on drivers' GPS location history and delivery records (personal data) to draft performance warnings that affect drivers. No legal, privacy, or AI policy review is recorded; 'Ops leadership supports the pilot' is not the required review.","evidence_quote":"Ops leadership supports the pilot.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/data protection, legal/HR, and generative AI policy reviews before launch, covering GPS data use and the human-approval flow."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of standard and design mismatch","detail":"The plan runs for 4 weeks, which meets the 14-day minimum, but the success metric target is set over 12 weeks, so the test cannot observe the stated outcome. Randomizing by market with no stated number of markets also leaves power unsupported, and drivers working across markets or managers handling multiple markets may leak between arms.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by market. Duration: 4 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align the experiment duration with the 12-week target, state the number of markets and how power was computed at the market level, and specify how cross-market drivers and managers are handled."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not fit the intervention","detail":"The problem is manager time spent drafting warnings, yet the success metric is Driver Safety Incident Rate. No metric measures drafting time saved, and the link between the warnings and safety incidents is not defined or justified.","evidence_quote":"Driver Safety Incident Rate: baseline 3.1 per 10,000 trips, target 2.6 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add a canonical metric for the stated problem (e.g., manager time per warning drafted) and justify the causal link to safety incidents, or reframe the success metric."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for driver-affecting warnings and LLM quality","detail":"Warnings can lead to driver discipline, but the only guardrail is earnings. There are no guardrails for driver attrition or retention, warning accuracy or error rate such as LLM hallucination or overridden drafts, driver disputes or appeals, or delivery completion and on-time performance.","evidence_quote":"Driver Hourly Earnings: must not fall below baseline.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for driver attrition, draft accuracy and manager override rate, dispute and appeal rate, and delivery quality metrics."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Time study claim lacks quantification and verifiable source","detail":"The claim that managers spend 'hours' drafting warnings is attributed to an ops time study with no figures, link, or date, so the problem size is unverifiable.","evidence_quote":"Operations managers spend hours drafting warnings to drivers with repeated service issues (source: LMD ops time study).","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the study with specific figures (hours per warning, number of warnings) and a link or date."}]}
